svg.text: How one HTTP request lives in memory: Spring Boot on port 5000 (Tomcat NIO + thread pool / virtual threads)
picks a READY TCB and loads its saved registers
(RIP, RSP, ...) into a CPU core = context switch
TCB = Thread Control Block (Linux task_struct / Windows KTHREAD). One per OS thread:

g.text: user stack ptr → its JVM stack
user stack ptr → its JVM stack
RSP → top frame of exec-1 stack

svg.text: ① accept() returns a new socket
JVM PROCESS (user space): java -jar EcommerceApp.jar, owns port 5000
(idle worker? run now : wait in queue)
virtual: new virtual thread per task
NATIVE MEMORY (outside the heap, not garbage collected)
one frame per method call; newest on top
call = push a frame · return = pop it
address of the NEXT instruction to run:
runs in order, jumps on call / branch / return
JAVA HEAP (objects, garbage collected, shared by all threads)
a parked virtual thread's frames are
copied here; the carrier thread is freed
Runnables waiting for a free worker
④ queued if no idle worker
the task exec-1 is running now
Singletons too: beans, JWT key, Caffeine
local variables in frames hold REFERENCES (addresses) of heap objects
class metadata + BYTECODE of every method: CartController.addToCart(), JWTFilter.doFilterInternal() ...
constant pools, method tables. Loaded once per class, shared by every thread.
The interpreter reads bytecode here instruction by instruction (PC = bytecode index).
Hot methods (JWTFilter, Jackson, Hibernate ...) are JIT-compiled by C1/C2 into x86/ARM instructions.
Once compiled, the CPU's RIP register points straight into this region.
Each instruction runs in order until a call (push frame), jump, or return (pop frame).
Tomcat runs each task on a NEW VirtualThread ("tomcat-handler-N"), a small heap object with no TCB of its own.
It is MOUNTED on a carrier platform thread (ForkJoinPool, ~1 per CPU core; that carrier has the stack + TCB above).
On blocking I/O (MySQL, ImageKit) its frames move to a StackChunk in the heap and the carrier is free for other requests.
control flow · highlighted = the thread serving this request
